releaseNotes:
1. Routine Line Patrol Tap-to-Edit: Tapping any saved card under Saved Works & Reports loads the complete patrol entry for viewing/editing (feeder, date, location numbers, work descriptions, before/after photos) with an active edit banner, Update Patrol Entry action, and independent delete.
2. Special Work High-Quality JPEG Export: Added 'Export JPEG' export option generating paginated JPEG image reports (<10 MB, adaptive compression, aspect-ratio preserved) with an interactive zoom viewer dialog, direct Save to device, and Share.
3. Overlapping Multi-Feeder Tower Selection: Tapping markers at identical/overlapping coordinates (<=5m) displays a compact feeder selection sheet with voltage badges and tower details, opening the selected feeder balloon tip without data cross-talk.
4. Bulk Marker Delete & Sequence Re-indexing: Added Delete button in the right feeder drawer multi-selection toolbar (Copy To, Move To, Delete, Cancel) with confirmation dialog and atomic SQLite transaction that updates polylines, re-indexes tower sequence orders, and refreshes cumulative distances.
5. Photo Metadata Integrity & Report Modernization: Camera captures acquire live GPS while Gallery imports strictly record null coordinates (no fake 0,0) and extract original EXIF capture time; historical records automatically migrated across Routine Patrol, Pre-Monsoon, and Special Work reports.

previousStableRelease.releaseNotes:
1. Crossings Abstract Excel (.xlsx) & PDF (.pdf) Export: Added filtered export (All/Selected Feeder, All/Selected Category) with 3-sheet formatted Excel workbook (Crossings Abstract, Crossing Details with frozen headers & AutoFilter, Import Template) and multi-page A4 Landscape PDF report with preview, Save, and Share.
2. Validated Excel Import & Safe Transaction: Exported workbooks can be edited and re-imported with row-by-row validation, duplicate/conflict detection, GIS route/dataset intersection protection (flagging unverified edits as Needs Review), Import Preview dialog, pre-import safety backup, and atomic SQLite transaction with audit history.
3. Voltage-Based Tower Marker Shapes: 230kV feeder tower Location Number badges now render as compact rounded rectangles while 110kV and other voltage levels preserve the existing circular badge, keeping alphanumeric labels (31A, 4T, 10/1T, 26/1) intact.
